name: Maurice Baring
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Maurice Baring (1874–1945) was an English man of letters, known as a dramatist, poet, novelist, translator and essayist, and as a travel writer and war correspondent with a particular knowledge of Russia.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: She listen'd to the music of the spheres
poems.author: Maurice Baring
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
She listen'd to the music of the spheres;
We thought she did not hear our happy strings;
Stars diadem'd her hair in misty rings,
And all too late we knew those stars were tears.
Without she was a temple of pure snow,
Within were piteous flames of sacrifice;
And underneath the dazzling mask of ice
A heart of swiftest fire was dying slow.

She in herself, as lonely lilies fold
Stiff silver petals over secret gold,
Shielded her passion and remain'd afar
From pity. Cast red roses on the pyre!
She that was snow shall rise to Heaven as fire
In the still glory of the morning star.
